haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If the hold lapses before claim, it expires by itself. At payment success, Inventory holds and claims again if stock is still free; otherwise the order is cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Inventory holds all lines in one step or nothing. If any line is short, Payment is never called, short items are shown, and the order is cancelled.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key on the charge request, so a repeat of the same request does nothing new and cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: The order is cancelled as out of stock, the customer is emailed, and Payment refunds the full amount with the order id. A refund that fails stays Pending and is retried.
haiku-low.q5: Cart empties only when Cart receives OrderConfirmed and the order is Confirmed. If checkout fails, the cart stays unchanged. Missed-event timing is an open question.
haiku-low.q6: Order drives the flow. It records each checkout's status (Placed, Reserved, Confirmed or Cancelled) in Order's own database.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment saves the outcome and publishes a Succeeded or Declined event on the broker, which Order subscribes to.
haiku-low.q8: Payment saves each webhook's event id in a table with a unique constraint. If the id is already saved, the repeat is ignored.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes Declined. Order receives it, sets the order to Cancelled, and calls Inventory to release the hold. The cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q10: By order status and stock. If already Cancelled, refund. Otherwise Inventory claims; if the hold lapsed and stock is free, it re-holds and claims, else refund. Always-refund is an open question.
haiku-low.q11: The refund stays Pending in Payment's database. The retry job resends it with the same order id until the provider accepts. Retry interval is not yet decided.
haiku-low.q12: Cart receives the OrderConfirmed event, published when Order sets the order to Confirmed, and then empties the cart. Cart is the service that clears it.

sonnet.q1: A hold lasts 10 minutes. If not claimed, it expires by itself (and a lapsed hold can be re-held and claimed again on success if stock is still free).
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before payment is requested. If any line is short, Inventory holds nothing (all or nothing), returns the short items, Order is Cancelled, the customer is shown the short items, no payment is requested, cart unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The order id is sent to the provider as the idempotency key, so a repeat cannot charge twice. (What happens when Order's own call to Payment times out is an open question.)
sonnet.q4: Order is set to Cancelled as out of stock, the customer is emailed, and Payment refunds the full amount (refund saved Pending, retried until the provider accepts). Nothing is deducted from stock.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is Confirmed (Cart empties it on receiving OrderConfirmed). If checkout fails for any reason, the cart stays exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: Order drives the flow. The record of progress is the order's status (Placed, Reserved, Confirmed, Cancelled), stored in Order's database.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which records the outcome and publishes a Succeeded or Declined event on the broker with the order id; Order subscribes and matches it by order id.
sonnet.q8: Payment first saves the webhook's event id in a table with a unique constraint; if already saved, the webhook is ignored. The constraint makes simultaneous copies count as one.
sonnet.q9: Order receiving the Declined event triggers it: Order sets status Cancelled and calls Inventory to release the hold. If the release call fails, the hold expires after 10 minutes.
sonnet.q10: If the hold lapsed and the stock is still free, Inventory holds and claims the lines again in the same transaction and the order is confirmed. If the stock is gone, nothing is deducted, the order is cancelled as out of stock and the full amount is refunded. (Whether to always refund instead is an open question.)
sonnet.q11: The refund stays Pending in Payment's database, and the retry job in Payment resends every Pending refund with the same order id until the provider accepts it. The retry interval is undecided.
sonnet.q12: Receipt of the OrderConfirmed event (published by Order) causes it; the Cart service empties the cart.
